summary.text: A previously healthy 42-year-old Bangladeshi male worker presented to the Hazm Mebaireek General Hospital Emergency Department in late 2023 with a 3-day history of abdominal pain, fever and intermittent vomiting, with no recent travel. He also had upper back and neck pain, ataxia, falls and inability to walk independently. On admission his abdomen was soft and lax with non-specific lower tenderness.

Workup showed high C-reactive protein, bilirubin, transaminases and lactate dehydrogenase, low platelets and a high INR, positive dengue virus IgG and IgM, and negative tests for Brucella, hepatitis A, B, C and E, HIV and COVID-19. Ultrasound and CT showed fatty liver changes, and MRI showed a posterior extradural collection compressing the thecal sac, considered most likely infective in origin. Platelet transfusions were started and hematologists evaluated him.

On day 3 post-admission he was transferred to Hamad General Hospital for neurosurgical intervention. Examination showed a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15, normal left-sided strength, right upper and lower limb weakness, intact sensation, a positive right Hoffman sign and urinary retention requiring a Foley catheter. On day 2 post-admission there he underwent right C7 hemilaminectomy with evacuation of an epidural hematoma, with significant postoperative improvement.

On day 8 he was transferred to the Qatar Rehabilitation Institute for active rehabilitation. On admission there his right lower limb strength was 3+/5 and he walked 150 m indoors with a minimal ataxic gait and contact guard assistance; FIM 110/126 and MMSE 30/30 were also recorded. He was discharged after 12 days of active rehabilitation; at discharge right lower limb strength was 4+/5, he walked indoors and outdoors with a slow gait, FIM was 122/126 and the disability scale score was 2.
